statBlock.specialAbilities:
SRD type: Giant

All giants speak Giant. Those with Intelligence scores of 10 or higher also speak Common.

Combat

Giants relish melee combat. They favor massive two-handed weapons and wield them with impressive skill. They have enough cunning to soften up a foe with ranged attacks first, if they can. A giant’s favorite ranged weapon is a big rock.

Rock Throwing (Ex)

Adult giants are accomplished rock throwers and receive a +1 racial bonus on attack rolls when throwing rocks. A giant of at least Large size can hurl rocks weighing 40 to 50 pounds each (Small objects) up to five range increments. The size of the range increment varies with the giant’s variety. A Huge giant can hurl rocks of 60 to 80 pounds (Medium objects).

Rock Catching (Ex)

A giant of at least Large size can catch Small, Medium, or Large rocks (or projectiles of similar shape).

Once per round, a giant that would normally be hit by a rock can make a Reflex save to catch it as a free action. The DC is 15 for a Small rock, 20 for a Medium one, and 25 for a Large one. (If the projectile provides a magical bonus on attack rolls, the DC increases by that amount.) The giant must be ready for and aware of the attack in order to make a rock catching attempt.

Special Attacks: Rock throwing

Special Qualities: Immunity to fire, low-light vision, rock catching, vulnerability to cold

Imported from the d20 SRD; verify attacks and skills in-game. Full rules at d20srd.org.
statBlock.organization: Solitary, gang (2-5), band (6-9 plus 35% noncombatants plus 1 adept or cleric of 1st or 2nd level), hunting/raiding party (6-9 plus 1 adept or sorcerer of 3rd-5th level plus 2-4 hell hounds and 2-3 trolls or ettins), or tribe (21-30 plus 1 adept, cleric, or sorcerer of 6th or 7th level plus 12-30 hell hounds, 12-22 trolls, 5-12 ettins, and 1-2 young red dragons)

system.biography:
Some fire giants have bright orange hair. An adult male is 12 feet tall, has a chest that measures 9 feet around, and weighs about 7,000 pounds. Females are slightly shorter and lighter. Fire giants can live to be 350 years old.

Fire giants wear sturdy cloth or leather garments colored red, orange, yellow, or black. Warriors wear helmets and half-plate armor of blackened steel.

Combat

Fire giants heat their rocks in a nearby fire, geyser, or lava pools, so that they deal extra fire damage. They favor magic flaming swords in melee (when they can get them). They are also fond of grabbing smaller opponents and tossing them somewhere very hot.

Rock Throwing (Ex)

The range increment is 120 feet for a fire giant’s thrown rocks.

system.description: You can strike two adjacent foes with a single swing.
system.benefit: As a standard action, you can make a single attack at your full base attack bonus against a foe within reach. If you hit, you deal damage normally and can make an additional attack (using your full base attack bonus) against a foe that is adjacent to the first and also within reach. You can only make one additional attack per round with this feat. You cannot use this feat if you are wearing heavy armor.
system.special: A fighter may select Cleave as one of his fighter bonus feats.

system.description: You can strike many adjacent foes with a single swing.
system.prerequisites: Cleave, Power Attack, Str 13, base attack bonus +4
system.benefit: As a standard action, you can make a single attack at your full base attack bonus against a foe within reach. If you hit, you deal damage normally and can make an additional attack (using your full base attack bonus) against a foe that is adjacent to the first and also within reach. If you hit that foe, you can continue to make attacks against other adjacent foes so long as you keep hitting. You cannot attack an individual foe more than once per round with this feat. You cannot use this feat if you are wearing heavy armor.
system.special: A fighter may select Great Cleave as one of his fighter bonus feats.

system.description: You are skilled at running down your opponents.
system.benefit: When you attempt to overrun an opponent, the target may not choose to avoid you. You also gain a +4 bonus on your Strength check to knock down your opponent.
system.special: A fighter may select Improved Overrun as one of his fighter bonus feats.

system.description: You are skilled at damaging your opponents' weapons and armor.
system.benefit: When you strike at an opponent's weapon or shield, you do not provoke an attack of opportunity. You also gain a +4 bonus on any attack roll made to attack an object held or carried by another character.
system.special: A fighter may select Improved Sunder as one of his fighter bonus feats.

system.description: You have a stronger will than normal.
system.benefit: You get a +2 bonus on all Will saving throws.

system.description: You can make exceptionally powerful melee attacks.
system.benefit: On your action, before making attack rolls for a round, you may choose to subtract a number from all melee attack rolls and add the same number to all melee damage rolls. This number may not exceed your base attack bonus. The penalty on attacks and bonus on damage apply until your next turn.

system.description: Check: With each successful Climb check, you can advance up, down, or across a slope, wall, or other steep incline (or even a ceiling with handholds) at one-quarter your normal speed.
You can use this skill to frighten opponents or to get them to act in a way that benefits you.
You can make running or standing jumps.
Your Spot check is either made against a DC that reflects how obvious the object is, or it is opposed by the target's Hide check.
Rock Throwing (Ex): The creature is an accomplished rock thrower and has a range increment as listed in its statistics.

What it does (SRD): In starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar dim lighting, the creature can see twice as far as a human can in the same light. It retains the ability to distinguish color and detail under those conditions that a human could not.

ThirdEra: Low-light vision is set on this item’s Details tab under Capability grants (vision and senses), not in Mechanical effects (no extra distance is needed for the usual reading of the rule). The character sheet includes it with other vision from items and race.

What it does (SRD): The creature can see in total darkness out to the distance set on this copy (default from the stat block). Darkvision is black and white only unless another rule says otherwise.

ThirdEra: Distance is under CGS parameters and overrides on this item (merged over the canonical template). The stat block’s distance is preserved when migrating from older packs.
